reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: Section 19.1 gives the professional/workmanlike and material-conformity warranties, 19.2 sets a ninety-day Deliverable conformity period running from the later of delivery or acceptance (plus full-term conformity for Hosted Services), 19.3 adds malicious-code and Applicable Law warranties, and 19.4 supplies re-perform/repair/replace with a refund backstop — matching the preferred position.

The failed deterministic check ('period >= 90 days or expressed in months/years') is correctly diagnosed as a formatting false negative: the period is written as 'ninety days', which equals the 90-day benchmark; the re-cite to Section 19.2 puts the period language on the face of the evidence.
No redline or counterparty comment is proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; nothing in the rendered redline alters the original paragraphs.

Section 19.5 confines the disclaimer to implied warranties and expressly states no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty and no carve-out edit is needed; 19.4 is also expressly non-exclusive for key claim types.

The rationale's disclosure that the malicious-code warranty reaches only code 'intentionally introduced by Vendor' is a fair, transparently noted narrowing but does not undermine the parametric period/remedy compliance; treating it as an internal note rather than a flagged deviation is defensible.
